name: Eric Clapton
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1971), Clapton had already been a member of the Yardbirds (1963-65), John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (1965-66), Cream (1966-68, four albums), Blind Faith (1969), and Derek and the Dominos (1970, Layla album). The 'Clapton is God' graffiti appeared in 1967, and he was widely regarded as the premier blues guitarist in Britain by his early twenties.
early_history_summary: Clapton received an acoustic guitar at thirteen and became obsessed with blues music, practicing long hours by playing along to records. He was expelled from Kingston College of Art for focusing on music rather than art. He joined the Roosters at 17, then the Yardbirds at 18 in October 1963, where he became one of the most talked-about guitarists in the British blues scene. He left the Yardbirds over their commercial direction and joined John Mayall's Bluesbreakers, where the influential 'Blues Breakers with Eric Clapton' (Beano Album) was recorded in 1966. He then formed Cream with Ginger Baker and Jack Bruce, achieving international fame with four albums before the band broke up in 1968.
family_context_summary: Born to 16-year-old Patricia Molly Clapton and a Canadian soldier who left before his birth. He was raised by his grandparents, believing his mother was his older sister. His mother later moved to Germany, leaving him in Surrey with his grandparents.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of musical family background; his grandparents raised him in a working-class Surrey household with no documented musical connections.
evidence_summary: Clapton grew up in difficult family circumstances, raised by grandparents in Surrey with no musical heritage. He developed an obsessive dedication to blues guitar from age thirteen, practicing relentlessly with a reel-to-reel tape recorder. The 1960s London blues-rock scene provided a frontier ecosystem: the Yardbirds' Crawdaddy Club residency connected him to the Rolling Stones' network, and his Bluesbreakers stint made him a guitar legend by 21. Key collaborative partnerships with Jack Bruce, Ginger Baker, and Steve Winwood multiplied his impact. By 26, he had been in five major bands and recorded landmark albums.
starting_point: Born to a 16-year-old mother in Ripley, Surrey; raised by grandparents in a working-class household with no musical heritage.
current_position: Semi-retired from touring; living in Surrey, England; estimated net worth ~$250 million; last major tour in 2023.

trajectory.title: Formed Cream
trajectory.description: Created the power trio Cream with Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, achieving international fame with four albums and extended blues improvisations.

trajectory.title: Cream disbanded; formed Blind Faith
trajectory.description: After Cream's breakup, Clapton formed the supergroup Blind Faith with Steve Winwood, Ginger Baker, and Ric Grech, recording one album before disbanding.

trajectory.title: Derek and the Dominos - Layla
trajectory.description: Formed Derek and the Dominos and recorded Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs, widely regarded as Clapton's masterpiece and a landmark of rock guitar.

trajectory.title: Solo breakthrough with 461 Ocean Boulevard
trajectory.description: Released his first solo album after overcoming heroin addiction; 'I Shot the Sheriff' became his first solo number-one single.

trajectory.title: MTV Unplugged and 'Tears in Heaven'
trajectory.description: Released the MTV Unplugged album featuring 'Tears in Heaven,' written after his son's death; won six Grammy Awards including Record of the Year.

trajectory.title: Grammy with B.B. King
trajectory.description: Collaborated with B.B. King on 'Riding with the King,' winning the Grammy for Best Traditional Blues Album and reinforcing his blues legacy.

name: Bjorn Borg
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first French Open title at age 18 in June 1974, the youngest male French Open champion at the time, having already made Sweden's Davis Cup team at 15, won the Wimbledon junior title and Orange Bowl at 16, and turned professional at 16 in 1973.
early_history_summary: Borg was born in Stockholm and grew up in Sodertalje. His father won a golden tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament and gave it to Borg, sparking his interest in tennis at age 9. By 13, he was beating Sweden's best under-18 players. Davis Cup captain Lennart Bergelin became his primary coach from 1971. At 15, Borg represented Sweden in the Davis Cup; at 16, he won the Wimbledon junior title and turned professional.
family_context_summary: Borg was born in Stockholm, the only child of Rune Borg (1932-2008), an electrician, and Margaretha Borg (b. 1934). He grew up in nearby Sodertalje in a working-class family. His father won a golden tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament and gave it to Borg as a child, beginning his tennis career.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was an electrician, not a tennis professional. However, his father's gift of a golden tennis racket won at a table-tennis tournament directly sparked Borg's interest in tennis, a serendipitous rather than planned domain transfer.
evidence_summary: Borg's tennis career was sparked by his father's gift of a golden tennis racket won at a table-tennis tournament, a serendipitous introduction to the sport at age 9. He showed extraordinary natural ability, beating Sweden's best under-18 players by 13, and was identified by Davis Cup captain Lennart Bergelin, who became his sustained coach from 1971 through his entire professional career. Borg's revolutionary playing style, featuring heavy topspin and a two-handed backhand, was so effective that Bergelin cautioned against anyone changing it. He was a teenage sensation who won the French Open at 18, propelled by the 1970s tennis boom. Despite a working-class background (father was an electrician), his prodigy-level talent and early coaching access drove his rapid ascent.
starting_point: Born in Sodertalje, Sweden to Rune and Margarethe Borg; father was a textile factory worker who won a tennis racquet in a tournament when Bjorn was 8.
current_position: Living in Stockholm, Sweden; fashion brand entrepreneur (Bjorn Borg brand); estimated net worth ~$40 million.

trajectory.title: ATP year-end No. 1

trajectory.title: Sixth French Open and retirement

trajectory.title: International Tennis Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, cementing his legacy with 11 Grand Slam titles in just seven years.

name: Michael Schumacher
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Formula One debut with Jordan at the 1991 Belgian Grand Prix at age 22, qualifying seventh, which led to Benetton signing him immediately; by age 25 he won his first World Drivers' Championship in 1994 and defended it in 1995.
early_history_summary: Born in Hürth, West Germany to a working-class family, Schumacher began competitive kart racing at age four in a pedal kart his father built from discarded parts. His parents took him to the Kerpen-Horrem karting track where he became the youngest club member. He obtained a Luxembourg kart license at 12 to circumvent German age rules, won the German Junior Kart Championship at 14, and the European Kart Championship at 18 in 1987. He dominated Formula König in 1988, won the German Formula Three Championship and Macau Grand Prix in 1990, and joined the Mercedes-Benz junior sportscar program before his F1 debut in 1991.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Hürth. Father worked at a karting track and built Schumacher's first kart from discarded parts, taking a second job renting and repairing karts. Mother worked at the track's canteen. Parents could not afford new engines; local businessmen provided financial support to continue racing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father modified a pedal kart with a motorcycle engine and built karts from discarded parts, worked at the karting track, and took a second job to support racing. Mother worked at the track canteen. Total family immersion in the karting environment, though not professional racing background.
evidence_summary: Schumacher's extraordinary racing career was built on early and total immersion in karting from age four, supported by a working-class family that sacrificed financially to enable his participation. His father built karts from discarded parts and both parents worked at the local karting track. Despite financial constraints (parents couldn't afford new engines), he progressed through the German karting system, won the European Championship at 18, and was recruited into the Mercedes-Benz junior program. Manager Willi Weber funded his Formula Three career, leading to his F1 debut at 22 and World Championship at 25.
starting_point: Born in Hurth, West Germany to a bricklayer father who ran the local kart track and a mother who operated the canteen; modest family background.
current_position: Living in Switzerland; health status closely guarded by family following a severe brain injury from a skiing accident in December 2013.

trajectory.title: First Ferrari World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his third World Championship and Ferrari's first in 21 years, beginning an unprecedented era of Ferrari dominance.

trajectory.title: Fifth World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his fifth title with a record 11 Grand Prix wins and a perfect podium rate, equalling Juan Manuel Fangio's long-standing record.

trajectory.title: Seventh World Championship
trajectory.description: Won his seventh and final World Championship with 13 race wins in 18 races, breaking numerous all-time F1 records.

trajectory.title: Second retirement from F1
trajectory.description: Retired from Formula One for the second time after a three-season comeback with Mercedes, having helped build the foundation for their future dominance.

trajectory.title: Skiing accident
trajectory.description: Suffered severe traumatic brain injury in a skiing accident at Meribel, France; has been receiving private medical care since.

name: Tom Hanks
milestone_by_age_26: Landed co-lead role in the ABC television sitcom Bosom Buddies in 1980 at age 24, which ran for two seasons and launched his career. Also made film debut in He Knows You're Alone (1980) and won the Cleveland Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in 1978 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Hanks was born in Concord, California to Amos Hanks (an itinerant cook) and Janet Turner (a hospital worker). His parents divorced when he was five and he moved frequently with his father around Northern California. He studied theater at Chabot College and Cal State Sacramento, then interned at the Great Lakes Theater Festival in Cleveland under Vincent Dowling, where he won the Cleveland Critics Circle Award in 1978. He moved to New York City in 1979, made his film debut in 1980, and was cast in Bosom Buddies.
family_context_summary: Hanks was born to Amos Hanks, an itinerant cook, and Janet Turner, a hospital worker, in Concord, California. His parents divorced when he was five. He grew up in various Northern California towns with his father and stepmother. No evidence of family wealth or entertainment industry connections in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of parental acting, entertainment, or artistic expertise. Father was a cook, mother was a hospital worker.
evidence_summary: Hanks grew up in a fractured family in Northern California; his father was an itinerant cook and his parents divorced when he was five. He discovered theater at Chabot College and transferred to Cal State Sacramento. His key break came when Vincent Dowling, head of the Great Lakes Theater Festival, offered him an internship that became a three-year immersion in all aspects of theater production. He won the Cleveland Critics Circle Award at 21, moved to NYC at 23, and landed the co-lead in ABC's Bosom Buddies at 24. No family entertainment connections or financial support were documented.
starting_point: Born in Concord, California to Amos Hanks, an itinerant cook, and Janet Turner, a hospital worker; parents divorced when he was five; grew up moving around Northern California with his father.
current_position: Active actor and producer; founder of Playtone production company; estimated net worth ~$400 million; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Presidential Medal of Freedom
trajectory.description: Received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Obama and the French Legion of Honor, recognizing his cultural contributions.

name: Zinedine Zidane
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1998 FIFA World Cup with France at age 26, scoring two goals in the final, and received the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year the same year. Previously won Ligue 1 Player of the Year in 1996 and Serie A titles with Juventus.
early_history_summary: Zidane grew up in the tough La Castellane neighborhood of Marseille, the youngest of five children of Algerian immigrant parents. He started playing football at age 5 on the local plaza, joined US Saint-Henri at 10, and was spotted by AS Cannes scout Jean Varraud at 14. He made his professional debut with Cannes on May 18, 1989 at age 16, transferred to Bordeaux in 1992, and to Juventus in 1996.
family_context_summary: Born to Algerian immigrant parents in La Castellane, a tough neighborhood in Marseille. Father Smaïl worked as a warehouseman and security guard at a department store, often on night shifts. Mother was a housewife. Youngest of five siblings. The family lived reasonably comfortably by neighborhood standards.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental football expertise or industry connections. Father worked as a warehouseman and security guard.
evidence_summary: Zidane grew up playing street football in the tough La Castellane neighborhood of Marseille, the son of Algerian immigrant parents. At 14, he was spotted by Cannes scout Jean Varraud at a French Football Federation camp and joined Cannes' training center, leaving his family. He made his professional debut at 16 and transferred to Bordeaux at 20, where coach Rolland Courbis became a father figure. His extraordinary technique was recognized early, but no family football connections or financial advantages are documented. The French football development pipeline and mentor coaches were critical to his rise.
starting_point: Born to Algerian immigrant parents in La Castellane, a tough neighborhood in Marseille; father Smail worked as a warehouseman and night-shift security guard; youngest of five children.
current_position: Former Real Madrid head coach; living in Madrid, Spain; estimated net worth ~$120 million; last managed Real Madrid in 2021.

name: Whitney Houston
milestone_by_age_26: Released her self-titled debut album Whitney Houston on February 14, 1985 at age 21, which became the best-selling debut album by a solo artist in history, topping the Billboard 200 for 14 weeks and generating three #1 singles.
early_history_summary: Houston joined the church choir at New Hope Baptist Church at age 5 and made her solo debut at 12 in November 1975. She began singing professionally at 14 as a background vocalist in her mother Cissy Houston's band at Manhattan cabaret clubs, and gave her first solo at Town Hall in February 1978. She became a teen model in 1980, appearing on the cover of Seventeen. She signed with Arista Records on April 10, 1983 at age 19 after Clive Davis saw her perform.
family_context_summary: Mother Cissy Houston was a Grammy-winning gospel and soul singer, member of The Drinkard Singers and founder of The Sweet Inspirations. Father John Russell Houston Jr. was a former Army serviceman and Newark municipal administrator. Cousins Dionne and Dee Dee Warwick were successful singers, cousin Leontyne Price was an opera singer, and Aretha Franklin was an 'honorary aunt.'
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a professional gospel and soul singer who trained Houston vocally throughout her teens. Extended family included multiple successful recording artists and opera singers, creating a deep musical dynasty.
evidence_summary: Houston was born into an extraordinary musical family: her mother Cissy Houston was a Grammy-winning gospel singer, her cousins Dionne and Dee Dee Warwick were successful recording artists, her cousin Leontyne Price was an opera singer, and Aretha Franklin was an honorary aunt. She began singing in church at 5, was trained by her mother throughout her teens, and turned professional at 14. This family-domain apprenticeship gave her both world-class vocal training and deep industry connections. She signed with Arista Records at 19 and released her record-breaking debut album at 21.
starting_point: Born in Newark, New Jersey to Cissy Houston, a Grammy-winning gospel singer, and John Russell Houston Jr., a Newark municipal administrator; cousin of Dionne Warwick and honorary niece of Aretha Franklin.
current_position: Died on February 11, 2012 at age 48 in Beverly Hills, California; final album was I Look to You (2009); inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame posthumously in 2020.

name: Jackie Chan
milestone_by_age_26: Starred in the breakthrough Hong Kong kung fu comedy films Snake in the Eagle's Shadow and Drunken Master in 1978 at age 24, establishing the comedic kung fu genre and propelling him to mainstream stardom across Asia; made his directorial debut with The Fearless Hyena in 1979 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Chan was enrolled at the China Drama Academy (Peking Opera School) around age 6 in 1960, where he trained rigorously for a decade in martial arts and acrobatics under Master Yu Jim-yuen, becoming part of the Seven Little Fortunes performance group. He appeared as a child actor in films from 1962 (age 8), worked as an extra and stunt double in Bruce Lee films in the early 1970s, and received his first leading role in New Fist of Fury (1976) at age 22 before his breakthrough in 1978.
family_context_summary: Chan was born to Charles and Lee-lee Chan, political refugees from the Chinese Civil War who fled to British Hong Kong in the 1940s. His father worked as a cook at the French consul's residence on Victoria Peak. The family was not wealthy; his father emigrated to Australia to work as a head cook for the American embassy when Chan was around 6.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence that Chan's parents had domain expertise in martial arts, performance, or film. His father was a cook and former secret agent; his mother's background is not documented in the performing arts.
evidence_summary: Chan's decade of training at the China Drama Academy under Master Yu Jim-yuen from age 6 provided exceptional physical and performance skills that were scarce even in Hong Kong's martial arts film industry. His immersion in the Peking Opera School system and early child acting roles gave him deep domain proximity from childhood. The Hong Kong kung fu film boom of the 1970s provided a structural wave, and his connections with fellow Seven Little Fortunes members Sammo Hung and Yuen Biao offered a complementary peer network. Family financial support was not a factor; his parents were refugees working in service jobs.
starting_point: Born in Hong Kong to Charles and Lee-Lee Chan, refugees from the Chinese Civil War; enrolled at age 6 in the China Drama Academy under Master Yu Jim-yuen, training in Peking Opera discipline for a decade.
current_position: Active in Chinese cinema; estimated net worth ~$400 million; received honorary Academy Award in 2016; films have grossed over $6 billion worldwide.

trajectory.description: Starred in the remake of The Karate Kid, his first dramatic role in an American film, which was a major commercial success.

trajectory.description: Received an honorary Academy Award for lifetime achievement, recognizing his extraordinary contributions to cinema across a career spanning more than 150 films.

name: Michael Jackson
milestone_by_age_26: Released 'Thriller' in November 1982 at age 24, which became the best-selling album of all time. Earlier milestones include four consecutive No. 1 Billboard Hot 100 singles with the Jackson 5 starting in 1969 at age 11, and the breakthrough solo album 'Off the Wall' in 1979 at age 21.
early_history_summary: Michael Jackson was born in Gary, Indiana, the eighth of ten children in a working-class African-American family. His father Joe Jackson, a crane operator at US Steel who also played guitar in a local R&B band, organized his sons into a musical group in the early 1960s. Michael began performing at age 5 and joined the Jackson 5 as lead singer. The group played talent shows and the Chitlin' Circuit, signed with Steeltown Records in 1967, then with Motown in 1968. Their first Motown single 'I Want You Back' hit No. 1 in January 1970. Michael launched his solo career with 'Off the Wall' (1979) and released 'Thriller' (1982), the best-selling album of all time.
family_context_summary: Born into a working-class African-American family in Gary, Indiana. Father Joe Jackson was a crane operator at US Steel who also played guitar in a local R&B band and became the Jackson 5's manager. Mother Katherine Jackson was a homemaker and Jehovah's Witness who played clarinet, cello, and piano. The family of ten children lived in a small two-bedroom home. Joe Jackson's management was reportedly physically and emotionally abusive.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Joe Jackson played guitar in a local R&B group (the Falcons) and managed the Jackson 5, providing both musical domain knowledge and relentless training. Mother Katherine was a aspiring musician who played multiple instruments and encouraged the children's musical talents. The entire family was organized around the musical group, making it a family business.
evidence_summary: Michael Jackson's extraordinary career was built on extreme early specialization: he began performing at age 5, was a professional recording artist by 9, and had four No. 1 hits by 12. His father Joe, a steelworker who played guitar in a local R&B band, organized and managed the Jackson 5 with intense (and reportedly abusive) rehearsal regimes. Signing with Motown, the premier Black music label, provided a world-class performance pipeline and national distribution. The Jackson 5 brothers formed a durable high-trust team, and Michael's prodigious vocal and dance talent was recognized from his earliest performances. Despite working-class origins in Gary, Indiana, the combination of family-domain apprenticeship, the Motown platform, and extraordinary natural talent produced the best-selling album of all time by age 24.
starting_point: Born in Gary, Indiana to Joe Jackson, a steel mill worker and former boxer, and Katherine Jackson, a Jehovah's Witness and former musician; eighth of ten children in a working-class African American family.
current_position: Died on June 25, 2009 at age 50 in Los Angeles, California, from an overdose of propofol administered by his personal physician; final album was Invincible (2001).

trajectory.description: Released Off the Wall, his first album with producer Quincy Jones, selling over 20 million copies and establishing him as a solo adult artist.

trajectory.description: Released Thriller, which became the best-selling album in history with over 70 million copies sold; won eight Grammy Awards and revolutionized music videos.

trajectory.description: Released Bad, the first album to produce five number-one Billboard Hot 100 singles; embarked on his first solo world tour, playing 123 concerts to 4.4 million fans.

trajectory.description: Released Dangerous, selling over 32 million copies; founded the Heal the World Foundation, reflecting his growing humanitarian focus.

trajectory.description: Released HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I, a double album combining greatest hits with new material, selling over 20 million copies worldwide.

trajectory.description: Died on June 25, 2009, from cardiac arrest caused by a propofol overdose administered by his physician, while preparing for a 50-concert residency in London.

name: Madonna
milestone_by_age_26: Released her debut single 'Everybody' on Sire Records in October 1982 and her self-titled debut album in July 1983, establishing herself as a recording artist by age 24.
early_history_summary: Madonna left the University of Michigan dance program in 1978 and moved to New York City with $35, training with Alvin Ailey and Martha Graham while working low-wage jobs. She pivoted from dance to music around 1979, playing in bands (Breakfast Club, Emmy) and building a following in the downtown NYC club scene, particularly at Danceteria, before DJ Mark Kamins helped her secure a deal with Sire Records in 1982.
family_context_summary: Madonna was born to Silvio 'Tony' Ciccone, an optical and military engineer at Chrysler Defense, and Madonna Louise Fortin, an X-ray technician. Her mother died of breast cancer when Madonna was five, leaving her the eldest daughter in a large family raised in the Detroit suburbs.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family background in music or entertainment; father was an engineer, mother was an X-ray technician. No evidence of parental domain expertise transferred to Madonna's eventual music career.
evidence_summary: Madonna arrived in New York with $35 and no music industry connections, having lost her mother at age five and grown up in a middle-class Detroit suburb. She leveraged immersion in the downtown NYC club scene—particularly Danceteria—to build a small but catalytic following, getting DJ Mark Kamins to play her demo and broker a deal with Sire Records. Her relentless hustle (living in rehearsal spaces, working multiple jobs, calling managers and labels daily) combined with the emerging MTV/dance-music wave of the early 1980s to create her breakthrough. No family financial platform or music-industry network was documented; her advantage was frontier geography immersion and adversity-driven urgency.
starting_point: Born in Bay City, Michigan to Silvio 'Tony' Ciccone, an optical and military engineer at Chrysler Defense, and Madonna Louise Fortin, an X-ray technician; mother died of breast cancer when Madonna was five; eldest daughter in a large family raised in Detroit suburbs.
current_position: Active performer and cultural icon; estimated net worth ~$850 million; completed the Celebration Tour in 2024, the highest-grossing tour by a female artist.

trajectory.title: Debut single 'Everybody' on Sire Records
trajectory.description: Released her debut single 'Everybody' on Sire Records in October 1982, launching her recording career from the downtown NYC club scene.

trajectory.title: Like a Virgin and MTV VMA performance
trajectory.description: Released Like a Virgin, her first number-one album and single; her iconic wedding-gown performance at the first MTV VMAs made her a pop culture phenomenon.

trajectory.title: True Blue - global superstardom
trajectory.description: Released True Blue, which reached number one in a record-breaking 28 countries and was named the best-selling album by a woman of all time by Guinness World Records.

trajectory.title: Like a Prayer
trajectory.description: Released Like a Prayer, her third consecutive number-one album, praised by critics as her most artistically ambitious work despite controversy over its title-track video.

trajectory.title: Founded Maverick Records
trajectory.description: Founded Maverick Records as a joint venture with Time Warner, receiving a $60 million advance and 20% royalties, one of the highest rates in the industry.

trajectory.title: Ray of Light - critical resurgence
trajectory.description: Released Ray of Light, produced with William Orbit, winning four Grammy Awards and marking a critical and commercial comeback that reinvented her sound.

trajectory.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
trajectory.description: Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, recognizing her as the best-selling female recording artist of all time with over 300 million albums sold worldwide.

trajectory.title: Celebration Tour
trajectory.description: Launched the Celebration Tour, her highest-grossing tour ever and the highest-grossing tour by a female artist in history, spanning four decades of hits.

name: George Weah
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for AS Monaco in 1988 at age 22 after being discovered by Arsène Wenger, was named African Footballer of the Year in 1989 at age 23, won the Coupe de France with Monaco in 1991, and helped Monaco reach the European Cup Winners' Cup final in 1992 before signing for PSG at age 26.
early_history_summary: Weah grew up in the Clara Town slum of Monrovia, Liberia, raised by his grandmother after his parents separated. He played street football and climbed through Liberian local clubs — Bong Range United, Mighty Barrolle, Invincible Eleven — before joining Cameroonian club Tonnerre Yaoundé in 1987. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who signed him for £12,000 in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Monrovia, Liberia, and raised in the Clara Town slum. Father William was a mechanic; mother Anna Quaye Weah died early. Raised by paternal grandmother Emma Klonjlaleh Brown. Extreme poverty; member of the Kru ethnic group from one of Liberia's poorest areas.
parent_family_domain_summary: No football or professional connections in family. Father was a mechanic. No domain-relevant transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Weah's path from Monrovia slums to European football was extraordinary. He had no family resources, no training facilities, and no football connections — he learned the game on dusty streets. Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy spotted him and recommended him to Arsène Wenger at Monaco, who became a father figure and mentor. Wenger's sustained coaching was transformative. Weah was named African Footballer of the Year at 23 in 1989. His extreme poverty and outsider status created the urgency and distinctive style that propelled him, but Wenger's mentorship was the critical catalyst that brought him to European football.
starting_point: Born in the Clara Town slum of Monrovia, Liberia; father was a mechanic and mother died early; raised by paternal grandmother in extreme poverty; member of the Kru ethnic group.
current_position: Former President of Liberia (2018-2024); living in Monrovia, Liberia; lost re-election in 2023; estimated net worth ~$30 million.

trajectory.title: Signed for AS Monaco
trajectory.description: Signed for AS Monaco by Arsene Wenger, who became a father figure and mentor, after being recommended by Cameroon coach Claude Le Roy.

trajectory.title: African Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named African Footballer of the Year for the first time, recognizing his explosive talent in European football.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Paris Saint-Germain
trajectory.description: Moved to PSG, where he won Division 1 in 1994 and became the top scorer of the 1994-95 UEFA Champions League.

trajectory.title: Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Became the first and only African player to win both the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year; signed for AC Milan the same year.

trajectory.title: Serie A title with AC Milan
trajectory.description: Won the Serie A title with AC Milan in his first season, finishing as the club's top goalscorer under Fabio Capello; won Serie A again in 1999.

trajectory.title: Retirement from professional football
trajectory.description: Retired from professional football after spells at Chelsea, Manchester City, Marseille, and Al Jazira, ending an 18-year professional career.

trajectory.title: Elected to Liberian Senate
trajectory.description: Elected to the Liberian Senate representing Montserrado County with 78% of the vote, becoming the first Liberian international athlete elected to the legislature.

trajectory.title: Inaugurated as President of Liberia
trajectory.description: Sworn in as the 25th President of Liberia, becoming the first African former professional footballer to become a head of state.

trajectory.title: Left presidency after electoral defeat
trajectory.description: Left office after losing the 2023 presidential election to Joseph Boakai, peacefully transferring power and reinforcing Liberia's democratic process.

name: Roberto Durán
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBA Lightweight Championship on June 26, 1972 at age 21 by defeating Ken Buchanan in 13 rounds, becoming the second youngest lightweight champion in history.
early_history_summary: Born into deep poverty in El Chorrillo, Panama, Durán shined shoes and sold newspapers from age 5. He began sparring at the Neco de La Guardia gym at age 8 and turned professional at 16 in March 1967, winning his first 29 fights. By 21 he was world lightweight champion with a 29-0 record.
family_context_summary: Born into extreme poverty in El Chorrillo, Panama. His father, Margarito Durán, was a Mexican-American U.S. Army cook who left the family when Roberto was young. His mother Clara raised nine children in a slum dwelling. Durán shined shoes and sold newspapers from age 5 to help support the family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family connection to boxing or athletics. Father was absent from childhood.
evidence_summary: Durán's path was forged in extreme poverty in Panama's El Chorrillo slums. He started boxing at age 8 at a local gym, turned pro at 16, and was world lightweight champion by 21 with a 29-0 record. His aggressive style and devastating punching power were honed through years of street survival and early gym sparring. No family resources or domain connections are documented; his rise was entirely self-driven, catalyzed by the urgency of poverty and natural physical talent.
starting_point: Born into extreme poverty in El Chorrillo, Panama; father was a Mexican-American U.S. Army cook who left the family; mother Clara raised nine children in a slum dwelling; shined shoes and sold newspapers from age 5.
current_position: Living in Panama; retired from boxing in 2002 at age 50; estimated net worth ~$5 million; widely regarded as the greatest lightweight boxer of all time.

trajectory.title: Professional boxing debut
trajectory.description: Made his professional boxing debut at Arena Colon in Panama City, winning his first purse of $25 and beginning a career that would span five decades.

trajectory.title: Won WBA Lightweight Championship
trajectory.description: Defeated Ken Buchanan in 13 rounds at Madison Square Garden to win the WBA Lightweight Championship, becoming the second youngest lightweight champion in history.

trajectory.title: Unified lightweight titles
trajectory.description: Stopped Esteban De Jesus in 12 rounds to unify the WBA and WBC lightweight titles, then vacated and moved up to welterweight with a 29-0 championship record.

trajectory.title: Defeated Sugar Ray Leonard; 'No Mas' rematch
trajectory.description: Defeated Sugar Ray Leonard by decision to win the WBC Welterweight Championship in June, then lost the rematch in November when he quit in the eighth round, infamously saying 'No mas.'

trajectory.title: WBA light middleweight title
trajectory.description: Won the WBA light middleweight championship, adding a third weight class to his world title collection.

trajectory.title: WBC middleweight title - four-division champion
trajectory.description: Won the WBC middleweight championship, becoming a four-division world champion and the first Spanish-speaking boxer to claim world titles in so many divisions.

trajectory.title: Final retirement
trajectory.description: Retired for good at age 50 following a car crash in Argentina that required life-saving surgery, ending his career with 103 wins and 70 knockouts in 119 fights.

name: Fernando Alonso
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2005 at age 24 (then youngest ever) with Renault, and successfully defended the title in 2006 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Oviedo, Spain to a working-class family, Alonso began karting at age 7. He won the CIK-FIA Five Continents Cup in 1996 at age 15, progressed to junior formulae at 17, winning the Euro Open by Nissan in 1999 and finishing fourth in International Formula 3000 in 2000. He signed for Minardi in 2001, making his F1 debut at 20, then joined Renault as a test driver before becoming a race driver and winning the world championship in 2005.
family_context_summary: Alonso was born and raised in Oviedo, Asturias, Spain, to a working-class family. His father was a mechanic in an explosives factory and his mother worked in a department store. The family made significant financial sacrifices to support his karting career from age 7.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in motorsport. His father was a mechanic, which may have provided some mechanical aptitude, but not racing-specific domain knowledge.
evidence_summary: Alonso's career was built on extreme early specialization — karting from age 7 with family sacrifices, progressing through a structured European junior formulae pipeline (Euro Open by Nissan, F3000) to F1. The karting-to-F1 pipeline is one of the most selective performance pathways in sport. His working-class background meant no financial safety net; the family's sacrifices and his talent combined to create urgency. The Renault team provided the complementary team structure for his championship wins. By 24, he was the youngest F1 world champion in history at the time.
starting_point: Born in Oviedo, Asturias, Spain to a working-class family; father was a mechanic in an explosives factory and mother worked in a department store; family made significant financial sacrifices to support his karting from age 7.
current_position: Racing for Aston Martin in Formula One; estimated net worth ~$240 million; first driver to reach 400 Grand Prix starts; contracted through 2026.

trajectory.title: F1 debut with Minardi
trajectory.description: Made his Formula One debut with Minardi at the Australian Grand Prix, becoming the third-youngest F1 driver in history at the time.

trajectory.title: Youngest polesitter and race winner
trajectory.description: Became the then-youngest polesitter at the Malaysian GP and youngest race winner at the Hungarian GP with Renault, announcing his arrival as a future champion.

trajectory.title: First World Championship
trajectory.description: Won the World Drivers' Championship with Renault, ending Michael Schumacher's five-year reign and becoming the first Spanish F1 World Champion and youngest champion in history.

trajectory.title: Second consecutive World Championship
trajectory.description: Successfully defended his title against Schumacher in a dramatic season finale, cementing his status as the driver who dethroned the Ferrari dynasty.

trajectory.title: Joined Ferrari; runner-up by four points
trajectory.description: Moved to Ferrari and finished runner-up to Sebastian Vettel by just four points in one of the closest championship battles in F1 history.

trajectory.title: 24 Hours of Le Mans winner
trajectory.description: Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Toyota, adding endurance racing's crown jewel to his F1 achievements; won the FIA World Endurance Championship the same season.

trajectory.title: Aston Martin resurgence and 400th GP
trajectory.description: Joined Aston Martin and scored eight podiums in a resurgent season; became the first driver to reach 400 Grand Prix starts, extending his record F1 career.

name: Kate Bush
milestone_by_age_26: Topped the UK singles chart for four weeks in March 1978 at age 19 with her debut single 'Wuthering Heights,' becoming the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song; her debut album The Kick Inside sold over a million copies.
early_history_summary: Bush began writing songs at age 11, taught herself piano, and grew up in a musical household in Kent. Family friend Ricky Hopper passed her demo to Pink Floyd guitarist David Gilmour, who financed a professional demo recording when she was 16. EMI signed her, gave her a large advance, and she spent two years studying interpretive dance before releasing 'Wuthering Heights' at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to a middle-class family in Bexleyheath, Kent. Father Paddy was a doctor and amateur pianist; mother was an amateur traditional Irish dancer. Two older brothers were heavily involved in music and poetry. Artistic household that encouraged creative development.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur pianist and mother an amateur Irish dancer; both older brothers were deeply involved in music. Family provided a rich musical environment and supported her artistic development from childhood.
evidence_summary: Bush's extraordinary songwriting talent emerged at 11, but the critical catalyst was David Gilmour of Pink Floyd, who personally financed her professional demo recording and connected her to EMI. Her family was middle-class and deeply musical — father a doctor and pianist, mother a dancer, brothers in music. EMI signed her at 16 and gave her a large advance for dance training. Her debut single 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK chart at 19, making her the first female artist with a self-written number one. The combination of mentorship, family musical environment, and label investment created a uniquely accelerated path.
starting_point: Born in Bexleyheath, Kent to a middle-class family; father Paddy was a doctor and amateur pianist, mother was an amateur Irish dancer; two older brothers deeply involved in music; artistic household that encouraged creative development.
current_position: Living in Devon, England; estimated net worth ~$60 million; largely reclusive but achieved massive resurgence in 2022; inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.

trajectory.title: 'Wuthering Heights' tops UK chart
trajectory.description: Her debut single 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK singles chart for four weeks, making her the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song.

trajectory.title: Never for Ever - first UK number-one album
trajectory.description: Released Never for Ever, which became her first album to top the UK Albums Chart, making her the first British solo female artist to achieve this.

trajectory.title: Hounds of Love
trajectory.description: Released Hounds of Love, her most critically acclaimed and commercially successful album, featuring 'Running Up That Hill' and the conceptual suite The Ninth Wave.

trajectory.title: The Red Shoes
trajectory.description: Released The Red Shoes, her seventh studio album, accompanied by a short film featuring Miranda Richardson and Lindsay Kemp; followed by a 12-year hiatus from recording.

trajectory.title: Aerial - return after 12 years
trajectory.description: Released Aerial, her first album in 12 years, a double album praised by critics for its ambition and intimacy, confirming her status as a reclusive genius.

trajectory.title: Before the Dawn concert residency
trajectory.description: Performed Before the Dawn, a 22-night residency at Hammersmith Apollo, her first live shows since the Tour of Life in 1979, receiving universal acclaim.

trajectory.title: 'Running Up That Hill' global resurgence
trajectory.description: After featuring in Netflix's Stranger Things, 'Running Up That Hill' became her second UK number-one single 44 years after her first, reaching number three on the US Billboard Hot 100.

name: Robin Williams
milestone_by_age_26: Made his national television debut on the 1977 NBC special The Great American Laugh Off and the Laugh-In revival series (1977-1978) at age 26, discovered by TV producer George Schlatter at the Comedy Store in Los Angeles, which led directly to his casting as Mork in Mork & Mindy (1978).
early_history_summary: Born in Chicago in 1951, Williams grew up in an affluent suburban family (father was a Ford senior executive). He attended private Detroit Country Day School, then Redwood High School in California. He studied theater at College of Marin for three years before earning a full scholarship to Juilliard in 1973, where he was one of two students (with Christopher Reeve) selected by John Houseman for the Advanced Program. He left Juilliard in 1976 and began performing stand-up at the Holy City Zoo in San Francisco, then moved to LA's Comedy Store where he was discovered by Schlatter in 1977.
family_context_summary: Father Robert Fitzgerald Williams was a senior executive in Ford's Lincoln-Mercury Division. Mother Laurie McLaurin was a former model whose great-grandfather was Mississippi senator and governor Anselm J. McLaurin. Family lived in a 40-room farmhouse on 20 acres in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. Comfortable upper-middle-class upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a corporate executive at Ford, not in entertainment. Mother was a former model. No direct family domain advantage in comedy or acting, though the family's social status provided access to private education and cultural exposure.
evidence_summary: Williams benefited from an affluent upbringing (father a Ford executive) that provided private schooling, and from elite training at Juilliard on full scholarship, where John Houseman selected him for the Advanced Program. The key catalyst was the San Francisco 'comedy renaissance' of the mid-1970s and the LA Comedy Store scene, which placed him at the frontier of a cultural wave. His extraordinary improvisational ability was recognized early by peers and teachers. The transition from stand-up to national TV via Schlatter's Laugh-In special in 1977 opened the door to Mork & Mindy and stardom.
starting_point: Born in Chicago, Illinois to Robert Fitzgerald Williams, a senior executive at Ford Motor Company, and Laurie McLaurin, a former model; raised in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan and Marin County, California; described as a shy, quiet child.
current_position: Died on August 11, 2014 at age 63 in Paradise Cay, California; autopsy revealed diffuse Lewy body disease; final films included Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb (2014).

trajectory.title: National TV debut
trajectory.description: Made his national television debut on the NBC special The Great American Laugh Off and the Laugh-In revival series, discovered by producer George Schlatter at the Comedy Store.

trajectory.title: Mork and Mindy breakthrough
trajectory.description: Rose to fame playing the alien Mork in the ABC sitcom Mork and Mindy (1978-1982), a role that originated as a guest spot on Happy Days and showcased his improvisational genius.

trajectory.title: First Oscar nomination for Good Morning, Vietnam
trajectory.description: Received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Actor for Good Morning, Vietnam, in which he improvised many of his scenes as irreverent radio DJ Adrian Cronauer.

trajectory.title: Dead Poets Society
trajectory.description: Starred as the inspirational teacher John Keating in Dead Poets Society, earning his second Oscar nomination and proving his dramatic range beyond comedy.

trajectory.title: Mrs. Doubtfire
trajectory.description: Starred in and produced Mrs. Doubtfire, a massive commercial hit that won him a Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy; also voiced the Genie in Aladdin (1992).

trajectory.title: Oscar win for Good Will Hunting
trajectory.description: Won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as psychologist Sean Maguire in Good Will Hunting, co-starring with Matt Damon and Ben Affleck.

trajectory.title: Death
trajectory.description: Died on August 11, 2014; his autopsy revealed diffuse Lewy body disease, a form of dementia that had been misdiagnosed as Parkinson's disease, explaining his severe depression and anxiety.

name: Jeff Bezos
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest senior vice president at D.E. Shaw & Co., a prominent Wall Street investment firm, in 1990 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Bezos graduated from Princeton University in 1986 at age 22 with a BSE in electrical engineering and computer science, summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa. He worked at Fitel (a fintech startup), then Bankers Trust, before joining the hedge fund D.E. Shaw & Co., where he rose to become the firm's youngest senior vice president at age 26 in 1990. This Wall Street experience and financial acumen laid the groundwork for his founding of Amazon in 1994.
family_context_summary: Bezos was born to a teenage mother in Albuquerque and was adopted by his Cuban-American stepfather Miguel Bezos, an Exxon engineer. The family moved to Houston and then Miami, providing a middle-class upbringing. His grandfather's Texas ranch fostered self-reliance and mechanical curiosity.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct family-domain advantage in technology or business; his stepfather was an engineer at Exxon, providing a middle-class stable environment. His grandfather influenced his practical tinkering instincts but was not a domain expert.
evidence_summary: Bezos's early trajectory was driven by elite institutional credentials: Princeton summa cum laude in electrical engineering and computer science, followed by rapid advancement on Wall Street. His middle-class family provided stability but not extraordinary resources. His early interest in computers and space (president of Princeton's SEDS chapter) combined with quantitative skills to make him valuable at D.E. Shaw, where he became youngest SVP at 26. The late-1980s Wall Street tech boom provided the structural wave that accelerated his career.
starting_point: Born in Albuquerque, New Mexico to a teenage mother; adopted by Cuban-American stepfather Miguel Bezos, an Exxon engineer; grew up in Houston and Miami; middle-class upbringing with grandfather's Texas ranch fostering mechanical curiosity.
current_position: Executive Chairman of Amazon; founder of Blue Origin; owner of The Washington Post; estimated net worth ~$284 billion; one of the wealthiest people in the world.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Princeton summa cum laude
trajectory.description: Graduated from Princeton University with a BSE in electrical engineering and computer science, summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, having been president of the SEDS space chapter.

trajectory.title: Youngest SVP at D.E. Shaw
trajectory.description: Became the youngest senior vice president at D.E. Shaw and Co., a prominent Wall Street hedge fund, gaining financial expertise and business acumen.

trajectory.title: Founded Amazon.com
trajectory.description: Quit his lucrative Wall Street job and drove cross-country to Seattle to found Amazon.com as an online bookstore, working from a rented garage in Bellevue, Washington.

trajectory.title: Amazon IPO
trajectory.description: Took Amazon public with an IPO at $18 per share, raising $54 million despite widespread skepticism about the company's profitability.

trajectory.title: Founded Blue Origin
trajectory.description: Founded the aerospace manufacturer and sub-orbital spaceflight company Blue Origin, pursuing his lifelong vision of making humanity a spacefaring civilization.

trajectory.title: Purchased The Washington Post
trajectory.description: Purchased The Washington Post for $250 million from the Graham family, transforming the newspaper's digital strategy and stabilizing its finances.

trajectory.title: World's wealthiest person; Whole Foods acquisition
trajectory.description: Became the world's wealthiest person as Amazon's market cap soared; acquired Whole Foods for $13.7 billion, marking Amazon's major push into physical retail.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Amazon CEO; flew to space
trajectory.description: Stepped down as Amazon CEO, becoming executive chairman; flew to space on Blue Origin's NS-16 flight, realizing a childhood dream.
